_why: Two functions named strip_column_ref_indices exist with the same stated purpose (ColumnRef{name,..} -> Column(name), recursive) and are ALREADY divergent. window_v2/strategies/general_row_eval.rs:172 takes &Expr, has a `_ =>` CATCH-ALL, and does not descend WindowFunction/OverClause. plan/physical_dispatch_resolver/plan_queries.rs:143 (added by #1994) takes Expr, is EXHAUSTIVE, and descends WindowFunction/OverClause/Subquery. The catch-all is the defect: any Expr variant added later is silently passed through UNSTRIPPED — no compile error, no test failure, just a ColumnRef surviving into a context that resolves by name, reading the wrong Arrow column against #1152's alphabetically-sorted inferred schema. That is precisely the two-hand-maintained-traversal drift the codebase's own rewrite_over_clause_with / expr_any / over_clause_exprs helpers exist to prevent, and their doc comments say so. #2029 cross-referenced rather than unified because making general_row_eval delegate to the exhaustive version changes what the window PER-ROW FALLBACK traverses — a behaviour change in the window hot path, inside a PR about HAVING binding. Verifying that behaviour change is safe IS the work, and is why this is its own issue.

anchors._note: the CATCH-ALL version. This one is DELETED. Its long doc block contains load-bearing #1724 reasoning and a pr-gate F2 BLOCKER rationale about Between/List — that prose must survive the move, not be dropped.
the EXHAUSTIVE version, #1994. This shape WINS. It has three helpers alongside it — _in_over_clause, _in_window_spec, _in_order_by — which move with it.

THE call site that determines whether the signature change costs anything. It calls strip ONCE PER BATCH (before iter_rows), not per row, and the existing &Expr version already deep-clones every node. So `strip(expr.clone())` against the owned version is the same order of cost — this is the measurement that makes the pinned design safe.

blast_radius._note: 45 refs / 3 files. Two are the implementations; the third (tests/unit/server/v2/partition_receiver_schema_inference_test.rs) only NAMES the function in a comment. Nearly all 45 are internal recursive self-calls inside the two bodies.

tests._note: fail_to_pass name indicative. This is a Chore, but it is NOT a pure move — the unified walker descends WindowFunction/OverClause/Subquery where general_row_eval's did not, so there IS a behaviour delta on the window path and it must be pinned by a test that FAILS against master. If no GeneralRowEval-reachable expression can contain a WindowFunction, that is a valuable NEGATIVE result: report it with evidence and say so instead of inventing a test.

acceptance: ONE strip_column_ref_indices exists, homed in the sql/ast.rs module alongside expr_any and rewrite_over_clause_with, with its three OverClause/WindowSpec/OrderBy helpers
it takes the EXHAUSTIVE shape from plan_queries.rs — no `_ =>` catch-all, so adding an Expr variant is a COMPILE ERROR, which is the entire point of the issue

the owned `Expr -> Expr` signature is kept; general_row_eval_batch_array passes expr.clone(). Justify this in the commit message with the measurement: the strip is once-per-batch, and the &Expr version already deep-cloned every node
both former call sites use it; neither file retains a private copy
the behaviour delta is stated explicitly in the report: the window per-row fallback now descends WindowFunction / OverClause / Subquery where it did not, and whether that is reachable in practice

the load-bearing prose from BOTH doc blocks is preserved on the unified function — the #1724 slow-path-not-wrong-answer classification, the pr-gate F2 Between/List reachability argument, and the cross-reference notes. Merge them; do not drop either
the two now-stale 'DUPLICATE — see ...' paragraphs are removed, since the duplication they warn about is gone
forbidden: do not keep the catch-all shape, and do not add a `_ =>` arm to the unified function 'for safety' — the exhaustiveness IS the fix
do not leave a thin wrapper or type-alias behind in either original file that lets the two drift again
do not delete the doc prose to make the move tidy. It records why the function exists and why two reviewers left it alone; it is the most valuable part of the diff
do not change ExpressionEvaluator, resolve_column_ref, or anything else general_row_eval calls
do not fix general_row_eval_batch_array's `.unwrap_or(FieldValue::Null)` — it swallows a real evaluation error and is a genuine defect, but it is not this issue. REPORT it
do not create a branch: the worktree is already on the branch velo-dispatch cut for you
stop_conditions: the unified walker's extra descent (WindowFunction / OverClause / Subquery) changes the output of any existing window test — STOP and report the test and the diff; that is the behaviour change this issue was carved out to evaluate, and accepting it is the maintainer's call

ast.rs turns out not to be an appropriate home (circular module dependency, or the Expr type is not visible there) — STOP and report where you would put it instead, do not silently pick a different module

more than ~10 pre-existing tests fail — STOP and report the list before changing any
